title: Variables, blocks, and lifetime: a state journal
goal: Trace variable creation, reassignment and the boundary of a block.

prerequisites.text: You can declare an int and compute a product.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: int total = price*count creates total and computes its initial value once. Later price=80 changes price but does not recalculate total. A separate total=price*count statement is needed.

Scope is the region of source where a name is available. A local name declared inside inner braces is visible only up to that block’s closing brace. The local int object lives until the end of its block; do not keep a pointer to use afterward. Initialize a number before reading it.

sections.title: Trace variable creation, reassignment and the boundary of a block.
trace: This initializes a new object with a number.
The variables are not linked by a live formula.
One stored old number and one new calculation.
Output occurs before local’s scope ends.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: After price=80, add total=price*count before output.
The new line assigns to the existing total; do not repeat int.
First 80×3=240 is stored in total; then both values print.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Using local after } is a name-visibility error; do not replace it by reading a new uninitialized number with the same name.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Create width=4, height=3 and area=width*height. Change width to 5; print the old area, then recalculate and print the new area.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? After price=80, add total=price*count before output.
selfcheck.feedback: The new line assigns to the existing total; do not repeat int. First 80×3=240 is stored in total; then both values print.

selfcheck.prompt: Create width=4, height=3 and area=width*height. Change width to 5; print the old area, then recalculate and print the new area.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. After width=5, the stored area is still 12. Only another area=width*height produces 15. Without recalculation, both lines are 12: a variable does not store an automatically updating formula.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Create width=4, height=3 and area=width*height. Change width to 5; print the old area, then recalculate and print the new area.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
After width=5, the stored area is still 12. Only another area=width*height produces 15. Without recalculation, both lines are 12: a variable does not store an automatically updating formula.

steps.action: Create width=4, height=3 and area=width*height. Change width to 5; print the old area, then recalculate and print the new area.

terms.definition: In these examples a named typed object with state; mutation is allowed unless the object is const.
Replacing the value of an existing object, as in stock = 7;.
The program region in which a name can be found under language rules.
The period in which an object exists during execution, rather than a source line or merely name visibility.
An inner declaration with the same name hides the outer declaration during lookup in that block.
